description_full: Nongfu Spring Co., Ltd. produces and sells packaged drinking water and beverage products primarily in Mainland China. It operates through five segments: Water Products, Ready-To-Drink Tea Products, Functional Drinks Products, Juice Beverage Products, and Other Products. The company offers edible ice; ready-to-drink tea beverages; functional drink products; fruit juice products; and other products, including beverage products, such as soda water beverage, coffee beverage, and plant-based beverages, as well as agricultural products comprising fresh fruits. It also provides supply chain management services, as well as engages in the beverage and IT research and development; and refined tea processing activities. The company was founded in 1996 and is headquartered in Hangzhou, China. Nongfu Spring Co., Ltd. is a subsidiary of Yangshengtang Co., Ltd.

financial_summary: NONGFU SPRING CO LTD. is a large-cap consumer defensive business with a $59.2B market cap on $7.9B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +14% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +2.9pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 73% against a 6% cost of capital — a 67-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat. Gross margins of 59% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $2.2B in free cash flow — roughly 27 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.33× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 2.2% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 64% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 4.8× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

sector_headwinds.text: Slow-motion taste and channel shifts — private label, Gen-Z health preferences, or a DTC disruption can erode decade-old brand moats without a single dramatic quarter.
Input cost inflation from agricultural commodities — when raw materials spike, pass-through pricing lags and margin compression is immediate.
GLP-1 and health-trend demand destruction — weight-loss drugs and wellness shifts are structurally reducing consumption in snack, beverage, and packaged food categories.
